title: Categorical processing of Chinese lexical tone: ECoG auditory oddball in 6 epilepsy patients (Si, Zhou & Hong 2017)
description: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from six patients with medically intractable epilepsy who passively listened to a two-deviant auditory oddball sequence of synthesized Mandarin /i/ syllables. The design contrasts a cross-category deviant (rising tone) and a within-category deviant (level tone) that are equidistant from a level-tone standard. It supports investigation of cortical networks for categorical processing of Chinese lexical tone. Data are organized in iEEG-BIDS without signal processing.
methods_description: ECoG was recorded with subdural grid electrodes using a g.USBamp amplifier at 1200 Hz with a 0.1 Hz high-pass and 50 Hz notch filter. Patients watched a silent movie while 500 oddball trials (250 for S6) were presented with an 1100 ms onset-to-onset interval and 5% jitter. Electrode placement was determined solely by clinical need.
